plan.title: AD lesional vs control: GO BP over-representation of DE genes
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question is narrow: which GO biological processes are over-represented among the genes called significant in the treated (AD lesional) versus control contrast. A DESeq2 results table for exactly that contrast is already delivered (/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv, 12,000 genes x 8 columns), so no new differential expression model is fitted — the plan takes the delivered table as its input and, per the rule for enrichment on a delivered results table, states the contrast, the reference level, the sign convention, the tie rule and the pinned collection.

Because the raw Salmon gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 12 samples plus the gene-symbol column) and the sample table (metadata.csv, 12 rows: 6 treated, 6 control, unpaired, single batch) are also delivered, T1S1 first runs a sample-structure check on them: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap and per-sample library sizes and detected-gene counts. This exists specifically because the profile flags sample_01 with a library size about 4x below the median. That sample is kept, inspected and reported — it is not dropped by default, and the QC step decides nothing about the DE table, which was computed upstream with all 12 samples. Its job is to tell the reader whether the delivered contrast rests on a sound sample structure, and whether sample_01 sits with its group.

T2S1 is the answer to the question: a hypergeometric GO Biological Process over-representation test with clusterProfiler enrichGO, with the universe set to the genes actually tested in de_results.csv (a non-NA adjusted p-value), never the whole genome. Significant genes are selected on the adjusted p-value at FDR 0.05, and the up-regulated and down-regulated sets are tested as two separate lists, with a pooled list reported beside them — an over-representation test on a pooled list mixes opposing directions into one term. Symbols are mapped to Entrez with org.Hs.eg.db and the unmapped share is reported. GO terms nest, so the significant terms are reduced to representatives with rrvgo semantic similarity and the full table is kept as a supplement. If fewer than about 50 genes pass the cutoff in a list, the step reports the list size and states that the hypergeometric test on it is underpowered rather than presenting terms as findings.

T2S2 is the robustness layer, kept separate so the primary answer stays clean. Counts-based DE lists are biased toward long and highly expressed genes; goseq refits the same GO BP question with a probability weighting function on gene length. The effective lengths from Salmon are not in the delivered files, so the step must obtain lengths from an available annotation resource, and if none is present it reports the bias uncorrected rather than substituting a wrong length vector. It also runs an fgsea preranked test on the full ranked list of every tested gene, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed ranking choice is resolved here in favour of the Wald statistic, which is signed and scaled by its standard error), explicitly as a stated secondary check and not as the answer.

T1S3 consolidates: the representative GO terms with their member genes and statistics, the overlap and the disagreement between enrichGO, goseq and fgsea, and the full reproducibility record — collection name and release, universe definition, size window, cutoffs, unmapped share, seed, package versions and sessionInfo.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
GO BP over-representation with clusterProfiler enrichGO, universe = tested genes, up and down lists separately plus pooled, rrvgo semantic reduction
goseq gene-length-bias-corrected GO BP over-representation as robustness check; fgsea preranked on DESeq2 Wald stat as stated secondary check
Consolidated report with collection version, universe, size window, cutoffs, unmapped share, sessionInfo and seed
